content.text: The verifier confirms the compliant classification is correct and that the failed numeric check (90) is a false positive keyed to our own termination-for-convenience notice. I'll resubmit with the rationale explicitly disposing of that figure.

input.quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
input.rationale:
Compliant at the preferred position. There is no automatic renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement: searches for "automatically renew" and "renew" return only p0065, under which maintenance runs "For a renewable one-year term" — a 12-month term extendable only by the parties' affirmative agreement — and the licence itself is perpetual so long as fees are paid (p0117). That matches the preferred position of renewal by mutual agreement on a 12-month term.

The ninety (90) day figure in p0118 is not a non-renewal notice window: it is Sparkling's own termination-for-convenience right ("Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman"). It is a customer exit right that benefits us, it is not a condition on renewal, and it belongs to a termination rule rather than this one, so it is not counted against the ≤60-day notice-window parameter.

Two sub-elements fall short of ideal drafting but are minor and noted rather than flagged: there is no express cap on renewal-period maintenance fee uplift (fees are simply "in accordance with the Fee Schedule"), and there is no vendor renewal reminder. We would pursue the CPI/3% uplift cap in the Fee Schedule negotiation rather than by redline here.
